transcript.en: So what I'm going to talk about to you today is something called Ethnography.
transcript.zh: 今天我要跟你们讲的是关于人种学的内容。

transcript.en: This is a type of research aimed at exploring the way human cultures work.
transcript.zh: 这是一种以探究人类文明如何起作用为目的的研究。

transcript.en: It was first developed for use in anthropology, and it's also been used in sociology and communication studies.
transcript.zh: 它起先是为了在人类学领域的使用而提出的，现在也被用于研究社会学和传播学。

transcript.en: So what's it got to do with business, you may ask.
transcript.zh: 你们也许要问，这跟商务有什么关系？

transcript.en: Well, businesses are finding that ethnography can offer them deeper insight into the possible needs of customers,
transcript.zh: 企业逐渐发现，学习人种学能够使他们更深层次地洞悉客户的潜在需求，

transcript.en: either present or future, as well as providing valuable information about their attitudes towards existing products.
transcript.zh: 不论是现有或未来的客户，同时也使他们获取了客户对他们现有产品的宝贵意见。

transcript.en: And ethnography can also help companies to design new products or services that customers really want.
transcript.zh: 而且人种学还能够帮助公司设计出客户真正想要的新产品或者服务。

transcript.en: Let's look at some examples of how ethnographic research works in business.
transcript.zh: 我们来看几个例子，看看人种学方面的研究是如何在商业中起作用的。

transcript.en: One team of researchers did a project for a company manufacturing kitchen equipment.
transcript.zh: 一组研究人员为一家生产厨房用具的公司做了一个项目。

transcript.en: They watched how cooks used measuring cups to measure out things like sugar and flour.
transcript.zh: 他们仔细观察了厨师们是如何使用量杯测算出像糖和面粉这类食品的用量的。

transcript.en: They saw that the cooks had to check and recheck the contents,
transcript.zh: 他们发现厨师们要反复检查量杯里的东西，

transcript.en: because although the measuring cups had numbers inside them, the cooks couldn't see these easily.
transcript.zh: 因为虽然这些量杯内部都有刻度，但是却无法轻易看见它们。

transcript.en: So a new design of cup was developed to overcome this problem, and it was a top seller.
transcript.zh: 于是他们设计了一种新的量杯来克服这个问题，而这种量杯也成为了最畅销的产品。

transcript.en: Another team of ethnographic researchers looked at how cell phones were used in Uganda, in Africa.
transcript.zh: 另一组人种学研究人员研究了非洲乌干达的人们是如何使用手机的。

transcript.en: They found that people who didn't have their own phones could pay to use the phones of local entrepreneurs.
transcript.zh: 他们发现那些自己没有手机的人，可以付钱使用当地企业家的手机。

transcript.en: Because these customers paid in advance for their calls, they were eager to know how much time they'd spent on the call so far.
transcript.zh: 由于这些顾客提前支付了打电话的费用，所以他们很想知道自己这通电话到目前为止已经打了多长时间。

transcript.en: So the phone company designed phones for use globally with this added feature.
transcript.zh: 于是电话公司设计出了能够在全球使用的，带有这项额外性能的手机。

transcript.en: Ethnographic research has also been carried out in computer companies.
transcript.zh: 计算机公司同样也进行了人种学研究。

transcript.en: In one company, IT systems administrators were observed for several weeks.
transcript.zh: 在某家公司里，他们持续观察了好几周IT系统管理员。

transcript.en: It was found that a large amount of their work involved communicating with colleagues in order to solve problems,
transcript.zh: 他们发现这些管理员的工作中很大一部分都涉及了和同事交流以解决问题，

transcript.en: but that they didn't have a standard way of exchanging information from spreadsheets and so on.
transcript.zh: 但是他们没有一个通过电子数据表之类的平台交换信息的标准方式。

transcript.en: So the team came up with an idea for software that would help them to do this.
transcript.zh: 于是这组研究人员提出了设计一个能够帮助他们做到这一点的软件的想法。

transcript.en: In another piece of research, a team observed and talked to nurses working in hospitals.
transcript.zh: 在另一次研究中，一组研究员观察并约谈了一些在医院工作的护士。

transcript.en: This led to the recognition that the nurses needed to access the computer records of their patients, no matter where they were.
transcript.zh: 他们发现，这些护士需要无论身在何处都能获取他们病人的电脑记录。

transcript.en: This led to the development of a portable computer tablet that allowed the nurses to check records in locations throughout the hospital.
transcript.zh: 这一发现导致了一种便携式平板电脑的问世，这个平板电脑使得护士在医院的任何地方都能查看记录。

transcript.en: Occasionally, research can be done even in environments where the researchers can't be present.
transcript.zh: 偶尔，在研究人员无法到达的环境里甚至也能进行研究。

transcript.en: For example, in one project done for an airline, respondents used their smartphones to record information during airline trips,
transcript.zh: 比如一个为航空公司进行的项目。受访者用他们的智能手机记录下了飞行过程的信息。

transcript.en: in a study aiming at tracking the emotions of passengers during a flight.
transcript.zh: 用于追踪乘客飞行时的情绪的研究中。

transcript.en: So what makes studies like these different from ordinary research?
transcript.zh: 那么这样的研究和寻常研究有什么不同呢？

transcript.en: Let's look at some of the general principles behind ethnographic research in business.
transcript.zh: 我们来看看商务领域的人种学研究背后的一些普遍原理。

transcript.en: First of all, the researcher has to be completely open-minded - he or she hasn't thought up a hypothesis to be tested, as is the case in other types of research.
transcript.zh: 首先，研究人员必须绝对虚心，他们不能像在其他类型的研究中那样事先想出一个假设，然后测试它的真实性。

transcript.en: Instead they wait for the participants in the research to inform them.
transcript.zh: 相反地，他们要等参与者自己展现出需要的信息。

transcript.en: As far as choosing the participants themselves is concerned, that's not really all that different from ordinary research - the criteria according to which the participants are chosen may be something as simple as the age bracket they fall into, or the researchers may select them according to their income, or they might try to find a set of people who all use a particular product, for example.
transcript.zh: 相反地，他们要等参与者自己展现出需要的信息。至于对参与者的选择，这和寻常研究并没有多少区别，参与者入选的标准也许只是一些很简单的事情，比如他们的年龄组或者收入，再或者研究人员也许会试着找到一群全都使用同一种特定产品的人。

transcript.en: But it's absolutely crucial to recruit the right people as participants.
transcript.zh: 但是征募到正确的人选作为参与者至关重要。

transcript.en: As well as the criteria I've mentioned, they have to be comfortable talking about themselves and being watched as they go about their activities.
transcript.zh: 除了我提到的标准之外，他们还必须对谈论自己的情况和有人观察他们做自己的事情不会感到不便。

transcript.en: Actually, most researchers say that people open up pretty easily, maybe because they're often in their own home or workplace.
transcript.zh: 事实上，大部分研究人员都说人们很容易对他们打开心扉，也许这是因为这些通常都是在他们自己家里或者单位进行的。

transcript.en: So what makes this type of research special is that it's not just a matter of sending a questionnaire to the participants, instead the research is usually based on first-hand observation of what they are doing at the time.
transcript.zh: 这种研究与众不同之处就在于它不只是给参与者发一份调查问卷而已，而是通常根据对参与者当时做的事情进行的亲身观察来展开研究。

transcript.en: But that doesn't mean that the researcher never talks to the participants.
transcript.zh: 但这并不是说研究人员从不跟这些参与者交谈。

transcript.en: However, unlike in traditional research, in this case it's the participant rather than the researchers who decides what direction the interview will follow.
transcript.zh: 不过，和传统的研究不同的是，在这种研究中，决定采访走向的并不是研究人员，而是参与者。

transcript.en: This means that there's less likelihood of the researcher imposing his or her own ideas on the participant.
transcript.zh: 也就是说，研究人员把自己的想法强加到参与者身上的可能性要小一些。

transcript.en: But after they've said goodbye to their participants and got back to their office, the researchers' workisn't finished.
transcript.zh: 但是在告别了参与者回到办公室之后，研究人员的工作还没有结束。

transcript.en: Most researchers estimate that 70 to 80 per cent of their time is spent not on the collecting of data but on its analysis - looking at photos, listening to recordings and transcribing them, and so on.
transcript.zh: 据大部分研究人员估计，他们百分之七十到八十的时间都花在了分析这些数据而不是收集它们上，他们要仔细看照片、听录音并转录它们等等。

transcript.en: The researchers may end up with hundreds of pages of notes.
transcript.zh: 研究人员最终可能会整理出数百页的笔记。

transcript.en: And to determine what's significant, they don't focus on the sensational things or the unusual things, instead they try to identify a pattern of some sort in all this data, and to discern the meaning behind it.
transcript.zh: 为了判定出重要的信息，他们不会把注意力集中在非同一般或者不寻常的事情上，而是试图辨认出所有数据中共同存在的某种模式，然后识别其背后的意义。

transcript.en: This can result in some compelling insights that can in turn feed back to the whole design process.
transcript.zh: 这一举动可能会带来一些引人注目的见解，而这些见解反过来能够反馈给整个设计流程。
